title: How Marc Lou built 21 products in 2 years: ideas from itches, 24-hour startups
summary: Marc contrasts a year-long $0 startup in 2017 with 10 launches making $263K in 2023. His speed playbook: source ideas from your own itches, shrink every startup to a 24-hour version, ship in a week or two with a buy button, and treat failure as repetition.

principles.text: Build ideas from your own itches and problems around you; the best products come from scratching them.
principles.quote: The most successful products were built by solopreneurs scratching their itches.

principles.text: At the start, building beats idea quality; shipping reveals real problems and better ideas.
principles.quote: When you get started, ideas don’t matter. Building them does. You’ll discover real problems and get tons of promising ideas.

principles.text: If no idea comes, do new things (sport, routine, skill) or solve universal problems like revenue and productivity.
principles.quote: If nothing comes, start something new. Try a new sport, start a new daily routine, or acquire new skills.

principles.text: Long build times inflate expectations and cause burnout; keep time invested low.
principles.quote: The more time invested, the higher the expectations. In the tough world of entrepreneurship where expectations are rarely met, spending months on a product is a recipe for burnout.

principles.text: Find the 24-hour version of your startup, cut non-critical features, and ship in 1-2 weeks with a buy button.
principles.quote: Find yours. Remove all non-critical features. Spend a week or two building. Write a good headline and ship with a buy button.

principles.text: Success is a series of small failures; be comfortable shipping imperfect work.
principles.quote: Building a successful startup is a repetition of tiny failures.
